text:
BLIND EDITORIAL ANNOTATION RUBRIC — SYNTHETIC TEXT

Read only the supplied document ID and text. Do not inspect creator requests, source code, prompt contracts, prior corpora, engine output, or another annotator's work. Do not call external APIs. Treat the source as a draft with its own natural communicative purpose. Do not invent an editorial assignment beyond what the draft supports.

For each document return a JSON object with exactly:
id, scope, feasibility, confidence, rationale, coupling, couplingRationale, jobs.

scope: LEAVE_ALONE | LOCAL | DISTRIBUTED_LIGHT | SUBSTANTIVE | AMBIGUOUS.
- LEAVE_ALONE: no material writing edit is warranted. Missing facts alone do not make the writing bad.
- LOCAL: one or a few independent passages can be improved.
- DISTRIBUTED_LIGHT: several passages need editing, but organization and information progression remain sound.
- SUBSTANTIVE: globally coupled changes to organization, progression, or repeated propositions are necessary; isolated edits cannot make a coherent good revision. Explain why in rationale/couplingRationale.
- AMBIGUOUS: the text does not support a defensible scope judgment.

feasibility: SAFE | PARTIALLY_SAFE | BLOCKED | UNDETERMINED.
- SAFE: all MATERIAL editing jobs you identify can be completed from source information, even if further facts would make the draft better. For LEAVE_ALONE use SAFE as a neutral value.
- PARTIALLY_SAFE: at least one meaningful material edit is safe now and at least one other material edit requires an absent fact. A single job can also be PARTIAL if part can be done now and part cannot. Identify both parts.
- BLOCKED: the core material improvement the document actually needs cannot be completed without an absent fact; merely trivial copyediting may still be possible.
- UNDETERMINED: available text does not establish the editing job or facts needed.

coupling: INDEPENDENT | PARTIALLY_COUPLED | GLOBALLY_COUPLED | NOT_APPLICABLE. Describe why the material jobs can be performed separately or why they depend on each other. Number of small local issues does not by itself imply globally coupled work. For no jobs use NOT_APPLICABLE.

jobs: 0..8 objects. Each has exactly:
- id: unique short string within document, such as J1
- operation: COMPRESS | REORGANIZE | CLARIFY | SIMPLIFY | DEDUPLICATE | SURFACE_EXISTING_INFORMATION | ADD_INFORMATION | OTHER
- objective: concrete editorial result, not "improve writing"
- scope: LOCAL | DISTRIBUTED | DOCUMENT_WIDE
- sourceEvidence: 1..4 exact substrings copied from the document. For a blocked job, cite the passage creating the need; no evidence can prove absence alone.
- feasibility: SAFE | PARTIAL | BLOCKED
- missingInformation: array of {proposition, necessity}, where necessity is REQUIRED_FOR_TRUTH or WOULD_IMPROVE. A partial/blocked job needs an exact REQUIRED_FOR_TRUTH proposition absent from the whole document. Do not use vague "more context".
- prohibitedInferences: explicit false or unsupported statements a rewrite must not infer, required for partial/blocked jobs.
- rationale: short editorial explanation.

Look for facts buried late, in headers, footnote-like passages, or under different job titles before calling them missing. Distinguish information REQUIRED TO PRESERVE TRUTH from information that WOULD IMPROVE THE DOCUMENT. Genuine deletion of redundancy, compression, and reordering existing facts can be safe even if cause, owner, metrics, or decision are unknown. Conversely do not create a cause, decision, owner, date, example, evidence, or outcome absent from the source. A clean incomplete status note may need no editing jobs. Do not force desired balance in labels. If you are unsure, lower confidence and explain.
